q: On January 1, Harlan Corp. issued a $1,000,000, 6% fixed-rate note and simultaneously entered into an interest rate swap (receive 6% fixed, pay SOFR) with matching terms, designated as a fair value hedge of the benchmark interest rate risk of the note. At December 31, benchmark rates had fallen and the swap had a fair value of $25,000 (asset); the fair value of the note attributable to the benchmark rate increased by $25,000. What net amount related to these fair value changes is recognized in Harlan's earnings for the year?
exp: In a fair value hedge (ASC 815-25), the $25,000 swap gain and the $25,000 loss from the basis adjustment to the hedged note are both recognized in earnings, so they offset to $0. Recognizing only the swap gain ignores the required adjustment to the carrying amount of the hedged item.

q: Ridley Co. designated a futures contract as a cash flow hedge of a highly probable forecasted inventory purchase. At year-end, the futures contract had a $40,000 gain. Under the prior rules, $3,000 of that gain would have been considered ineffective. Under current ASC 815 guidance, how much of the gain is reported in other comprehensive income at year-end, assuming the hedge remains highly effective?
exp: After ASU 2017-12, the entire change in fair value of a hedging instrument included in the effectiveness assessment of a highly effective cash flow hedge is recorded in OCI, so all $40,000 is deferred; ineffectiveness is no longer separately measured. The $37,000 answer applies the superseded rule that sent the ineffective portion to earnings.

q: On November 1, Benton Inc. entered into a 90-day forward contract to purchase 100,000 euros at a forward rate of $1.10. The contract was not designated as a hedge. On December 31, the forward rate for a contract maturing on the original settlement date was $1.14. Ignoring discounting, how should Benton report the forward contract in its December 31 financial statements?
choices: No amount, because the contract is executory
A $4,000 gain in other comprehensive income
exp: An undesignated derivative is measured at fair value with changes in earnings: 100,000 x ($1.14 - $1.10) = $4,000 gain, since the right to buy euros at $1.10 is worth more when the forward rate rises. OCI treatment applies only to qualifying cash flow or net investment hedges.

q: Delmar Co. purchased a call option on 1,000 shares of Zeta stock with a strike price of $50 for a premium of $3,000 when Zeta was trading at $50. At year-end, Zeta traded at $56 and the option had a fair value of $8,500. The option is not designated as a hedge. What gain should Delmar recognize in earnings for the year?
exp: The option is carried at fair value: $8,500 - $3,000 premium paid = $5,500 gain in earnings. The $6,000 figure is only the intrinsic value change and ignores that the $3,000 time value at purchase declined to $2,500.

q: Fenwick Corp. holds silver inventory with a cost of $200,000 and designated short silver futures as a fair value hedge of the inventory's price risk. During the period, the fair value of the inventory declined by $15,000 and the futures contracts gained $14,000. What is the net effect on Fenwick's earnings for the period?
exp: In a fair value hedge, the hedged inventory is adjusted for the $15,000 decline (loss in earnings) and the futures gain of $14,000 is also in earnings, netting to a $1,000 decrease. Ignoring the inventory basis adjustment would show only the $14,000 gain.

q: Gale Co. had a $40,000 gain in accumulated other comprehensive income from a cash flow hedge of a forecasted inventory purchase. The inventory was purchased in March, and 60% of it was sold by year-end. How much of the deferred gain should be reclassified from AOCI to earnings during the year?
exp: Amounts in AOCI are reclassified when the hedged forecasted transaction affects earnings; for inventory that is when it is sold through cost of goods sold: $40,000 x 60% = $24,000. Reclassifying all $40,000 at purchase date is the common trap—the purchase itself does not affect earnings.

q: Hollis Inc. has $5,000,000 of variable-rate debt bearing interest at SOFR + 1%. It entered into a swap to pay 4% fixed and receive SOFR on $5,000,000, designated as a cash flow hedge. SOFR averaged 3.2% for the year. What total interest expense, including the swap net settlement, should Hollis report?
exp: Debt interest is $5,000,000 x 4.2% = $210,000; the swap requires paying 4% and receiving 3.2%, a net payment of $5,000,000 x 0.8% = $40,000, for total interest of $250,000 (an effective 5% fixed rate). Stopping at $210,000 ignores the swap settlement that converts the debt to fixed.

q: Irving Co. has a $2,000,000, 6% fixed-rate note. It entered into a swap to receive 5% fixed and pay SOFR on a $2,000,000 notional, designated as a fair value hedge. SOFR for the year was 3.5%. Ignoring any fair value changes, what is Irving's net interest expense for the year?
exp: Note interest is $120,000; the swap receives $100,000 (5%) and pays $70,000 (3.5%), a net receipt of $30,000, so net interest is $120,000 - $30,000 = $90,000 (effectively SOFR + 1%). Answering $70,000 counts only the SOFR leg and ignores the 1% spread between the note coupon and the swap's fixed leg.

q: Jessup Corp. firmly committed to buy equipment for 500,000 euros with delivery in three months and entered into a forward contract to buy 500,000 euros at $1.12, designated as a fair value hedge of the firm commitment (effectiveness based on forward rates). On the delivery date, the spot rate was $1.15. At what amount should Jessup record the equipment?
exp: The forward gain of 500,000 x ($1.15 - $1.12) = $15,000 is offset by a $15,000 firm commitment liability, which is closed against the equipment: $575,000 cash price - $15,000 = $560,000, locking in the forward rate. Recording $575,000 ignores the firm commitment basis adjustment required in a fair value hedge.

q: Kimball Co. issued a five-year note whose principal repayment at maturity equals $1,000,000 adjusted by the percentage change in the S&P 500 index over the note's term. Which treatment does ASC 815 require for this feature?
choices: Account for the entire note at amortized cost because the index is a widely published market measure
Bifurcate the equity-index feature and account for it as a derivative because it is not clearly and closely related to the debt host
Record the index feature in additional paid-in capital as an equity component
Bifurcate only if the note is convertible into Kimball's own shares
exp: An equity-indexed principal payment has economic characteristics unrelated to a debt host, so the embedded derivative is not clearly and closely related and must be separated and measured at fair value (ASC 815-15), unless the fair value option is elected for the whole instrument. Being a published index does not make it closely related to interest rates or credit.

q: Lyman Inc. uses the dollar-offset method to assess hedge effectiveness. For the quarter, the change in fair value of the hedged item attributable to the hedged risk was a $100,000 decrease, and the hedging derivative increased $88,000. What is the offset ratio and conclusion?
choices: 88%; not highly effective because the ratio is below 90%
exp: The offset ratio is $88,000 / $100,000 = 88%, which falls within the 80%-125% range generally accepted as highly effective. The 90% threshold is not part of the guidance, and 112% inverts the ratio but would still be within range.

q: Marlow Corp. (USD functional currency) has a net investment of 10 million euros in a German subsidiary and designated 10 million euros of borrowings as a hedge of that net investment. During the year the euro strengthened from $1.10 to $1.15. How is the remeasurement of the euro debt reported?
choices: $500,000 loss in other comprehensive income as part of the cumulative translation adjustment
exp: The euro debt increases by 10,000,000 x $0.05 = $500,000; as an effective net investment hedge, the loss goes to the CTA in OCI, offsetting the translation gain on the net investment (ASC 815-35). Reporting it in net income ignores the designated hedge relationship.

q: Norris Co. entered into a 6-month forward contract to sell 1,000,000 Swiss francs at $1.08. At year-end, three months remain and the forward rate for that settlement date is $1.05. The appropriate discount rate is 8% per year (simple interest). What is the fair value of the forward contract at year-end?
exp: The undiscounted gain is 1,000,000 x ($1.08 - $1.05) = $30,000, receivable in 3 months; discounting gives $30,000 / (1 + 0.08 x 3/12) = $30,000 / 1.02 = $29,412. The $27,778 answer discounts for a full year instead of three months.

q: Oakes Co. purchased an at-the-money currency option for a $12,000 premium (all time value) and designated it as a cash flow hedge of a forecasted purchase 12 months away. It excluded time value from the effectiveness assessment and elected to recognize the excluded component in earnings using a systematic and rational amortization approach. The option was purchased September 1. How much of the excluded component is recognized in earnings for the year ended December 31?
exp: Under ASU 2017-12, the initial value of an excluded component may be amortized into earnings over the hedge term: $12,000 x 4/12 = $4,000 for September through December. Recognizing $0 would defer the entire time value in OCI, which the amortization election does not allow.

q: Pruitt Farms bought five corn futures contracts of 5,000 bushels each at $4.50 per bushel and posted initial margin of $2,000 per contract. The contracts were not designated as hedges. At year-end, the futures price was $4.30. What should Pruitt report in earnings?
choices: $0, because only the margin deposit has been paid
exp: The futures loss is 25,000 bushels x ($4.50 - $4.30) = $5,000, recognized in earnings because the contracts are undesignated derivatives. The margin deposit is a separate asset, and $1,000 uses only one contract's bushels.

q: Quinlan Corp. has a $30,000 gain in AOCI from a cash flow hedge of a forecasted sale. Quinlan discontinued hedge accounting because the forecasted sale is no longer probable, though it is still reasonably possible that it will occur within an additional two months. How much of the AOCI gain should be reclassified to earnings immediately?
choices: $0; the gain remains in AOCI until the forecasted transaction affects earnings or becomes probable of not occurring
$15,000 to earnings, with the remainder in AOCI
exp: Under ASC 815-30-40, amounts stay in AOCI after discontinuance unless it is probable that the forecasted transaction will not occur within the original period or the additional two-month window. Immediate reclassification is the trap; it is required only when occurrence becomes probable of not happening.

q: Ross Co. holds an available-for-sale fixed-rate debt security and designated a swap as a fair value hedge of its benchmark interest rate risk. During the year, the security's fair value fell $50,000, of which $42,000 was attributable to the benchmark rate and $8,000 to other non-credit factors. The swap gained $41,000. What is the effect on Ross's net income?
exp: In a fair value hedge of an AFS security, the change attributable to the hedged risk ($42,000 loss) moves from OCI to earnings and offsets the $41,000 swap gain, a $1,000 decrease; the $8,000 unhedged change stays in OCI. The $9,000 answer puts the entire security decline in earnings.

q: Sutton Inc. wrote a put option on 1,000 shares of a listed stock and received a $5,000 premium. At year-end, the fair value of the written option was $9,000. The option is not a hedge. What should Sutton recognize in earnings for the year?
exp: The written option is a liability initially recorded at the $5,000 premium and remeasured to $9,000, producing a $4,000 loss. Recognizing the premium as a $5,000 gain ignores that it is a liability carried at fair value.

q: Taft Co. designated a receive-fixed, pay-variable swap as a fair value hedge of its fixed-rate debt. Under current ASC 815 presentation requirements, where is the change in the swap's fair value reported in the income statement?
choices: Other income, separate from the hedged item
Interest expense, the same line as the earnings effect of the hedged debt
A separate hedging gains and losses line below operating income
exp: ASU 2017-12 requires the change in fair value of a fair value hedging instrument to be presented in the same income statement line as the earnings effect of the hedged item—here, interest expense. OCI is used for cash flow and net investment hedges, not fair value hedges.

q: Underwood Corp. wants to apply the shortcut method to a receive-fixed, pay-SOFR swap hedging its fixed-rate debt. Which fact would preclude use of the shortcut method?
choices: The swap's notional amount equals the debt's principal
The swap's expiration date matches the debt's maturity
The swap had a fair value of $40,000 at inception because its fixed rate was off-market
The variable leg of the swap is indexed to SOFR
exp: The shortcut method requires the swap's fair value at inception to be zero (ASC 815-20-25-104); an off-market swap with a $40,000 initial value fails that condition. Matching notional, matching maturity, and a benchmark variable rate such as SOFR are all consistent with the shortcut method.

q: In October, Vance Airlines bought futures for 50,000 gallons of jet fuel at $2.40 per gallon, designated as a cash flow hedge of a March fuel purchase. At December 31, the futures price was $2.60. In March, Vance bought the fuel at the spot price of $2.75 and closed the futures at $2.75. When the fuel is consumed, what total fuel expense is recognized?
exp: The total futures gain is 50,000 x ($2.75 - $2.40) = $17,500, deferred in AOCI and reclassified when the fuel is consumed: $137,500 - $17,500 = $120,000 (the locked-in $2.40 price). The $127,500 answer offsets only the $10,000 gain recorded through December 31.

q: Walsh Co. has an interest rate swap with a $10,000,000 notional amount under which it pays 3.5% fixed and receives SOFR. For the current annual period, SOFR was reset at 4.1%. What is the net settlement for the period?
exp: Walsh receives 4.1% and pays 3.5%, so it receives the net 0.6% x $10,000,000 = $60,000; swaps settle net rather than gross. Paying $60,000 reverses the direction of the legs.

q: Yardley Inc. designated a forward contract to sell 100,000,000 yen at $0.0070 as a cash flow hedge of a forecasted yen-denominated sale. The sale occurred when the spot rate was $0.0066, and the forward was settled at that date. What total revenue does Yardley report for the sale, including amounts reclassified from AOCI?
exp: Revenue at spot is 100,000,000 x $0.0066 = $660,000; the forward gain of 100,000,000 x $0.0004 = $40,000 is reclassified from AOCI into revenue when the sale affects earnings, for $700,000 total—the hedged rate. The $620,000 answer subtracts the gain instead of adding it.

q: Zeller Corp., a public business entity, entered into an interest rate swap on January 1 to hedge fixed-rate debt but did not prepare formal hedge documentation until March 31. Between January 1 and March 31, the swap's fair value increased $18,000 and the fair value of the debt attributable to the benchmark rate increased $18,000. What is the effect on Zeller's first-quarter earnings?
exp: Hedge accounting applies only from the date formal documentation is in place, so for January through March the swap is an undesignated derivative and its $18,000 gain goes to earnings with no offsetting basis adjustment on the debt. Answering $0 assumes hedge accounting was available retroactively.

q: Which of the following contracts entered into by Abbott Manufacturing is accounted for as a derivative under ASC 815?
choices: A contract to buy steel for use in production with physical delivery in quantities expected to be used, documented under the normal purchases exception
A forward contract to buy shares of a privately held company requiring gross physical delivery, with no market mechanism to settle net
Stock options granted to employees as compensation
A five-year interest rate swap with a $5,000,000 notional amount and no initial payment
exp: The swap has an underlying and notional amount, no initial net investment, and settles net, meeting the ASC 815-10-15-83 definition. The steel contract qualifies for the normal purchases scope exception, the private-share forward fails net settlement, and employee share-based awards are in ASC 718's scope.

q: Baxter Co. entered into a pay-fixed, receive-SOFR swap as a highly effective cash flow hedge of its variable-rate debt. Rates rose during the year, and at December 31 the swap had a fair value of $75,000 (asset). Baxter's tax rate is 25%. Assuming no reclassifications, what amount should be in AOCI related to the swap at December 31, net of tax?
exp: The $75,000 swap gain is deferred in OCI for an effective cash flow hedge and presented net of deferred tax: $75,000 x (1 - 25%) = $56,250. The $75,000 answer ignores the related deferred tax effect.

q: Carver Corp. has variable-rate debt and has designated a pay-fixed, receive-variable swap as a cash flow hedge. If market interest rates decline significantly, how is the swap affected?
choices: The swap becomes an asset, with the gain recognized in earnings
The swap becomes a liability, with the loss deferred in other comprehensive income
The swap becomes a liability, with the loss recognized as an adjustment to the debt's carrying amount
The swap's fair value does not change because the debt rate also declines
exp: When rates fall, paying fixed and receiving a lower variable rate is unfavorable, so the swap becomes a liability; in an effective cash flow hedge the loss goes to OCI and is reclassified as interest is paid. Adjusting the debt's carrying amount is a fair value hedge treatment.

q: Dunn Oil entered into a monthly commodity swap on 10,000 barrels under which it pays a fixed $80 per barrel and receives the average index price. For the current month, the average index price was $86 per barrel. What is the net settlement for the month?
exp: Dunn receives $86 and pays $80 per barrel, a net receipt of 10,000 x $6 = $60,000; the swap settles net, not gross. Paying $60,000 reverses the direction of the legs.

q: Which of the following hedging relationships is prohibited from receiving hedge accounting under ASC 815?
choices: A cash flow hedge of variable interest receipts on an available-for-sale debt security
A fair value hedge of interest rate risk on fixed-rate debt issued by the entity
A net investment hedge using foreign-currency-denominated debt
A fair value hedge of the interest rate risk of a held-to-maturity debt security
exp: ASC 815-20-25-43 prohibits designating interest rate risk of a held-to-maturity security as the hedged risk, since the entity has asserted it will hold the security to maturity regardless of rate changes (hedging the prepayment option component is the narrow exception). The other relationships are all eligible.

q: On December 1, Ellery Co. sold goods for 200,000 British pounds on 60-day credit when the spot rate was $1.25 and simultaneously entered into a 60-day forward contract to sell 200,000 pounds at $1.24 (not designated as a hedge). At December 31, the spot rate was $1.22 and the forward rate for the remaining 30 days was $1.215. Ignoring discounting, what is the net effect on December earnings?
exp: The receivable loses 200,000 x ($1.25 - $1.22) = $6,000 (spot rate remeasurement), and the forward gains 200,000 x ($1.24 - $1.215) = $5,000, for a net $1,000 loss. Reporting only the $6,000 receivable loss ignores the forward that acts as a natural hedge through earnings.

q: Before issuing 10-year fixed-rate bonds, Finch Corp. entered into a treasury lock designated as a cash flow hedge of the forecasted interest payments. Rates rose before issuance, and Finch settled the lock for a $120,000 gain, which was deferred in AOCI. Assuming the gain is reclassified in equal annual amounts as a yield adjustment, how does the gain affect the first full year after issuance?
choices: Interest expense is reduced by $120,000 at issuance
Other income of $120,000 is recognized at settlement
exp: The deferred gain is reclassified from AOCI as the hedged interest payments affect earnings, reducing interest expense by about $120,000 / 10 = $12,000 per year. Recognizing the full gain at settlement ignores that the hedged transactions are the future interest payments.

q: Gilman Inc. issued a hybrid debt instrument for $1,000,000 cash. Gilman determined that an embedded derivative must be bifurcated and that its fair value at issuance is $70,000. At what amount should the host debt contract be initially recorded?
exp: The embedded derivative is recorded at fair value, and the host contract receives the residual: $1,000,000 - $70,000 = $930,000, with the difference accreted as additional interest. Adding the derivative value to proceeds reverses the with-and-without allocation.

q: Harper Co. has an interest rate swap with two annual settlements remaining on a $1,000,000 notional, under which it receives 5% fixed and pays a variable rate. The market expects the variable rate to be 4% for both remaining years, and the appropriate discount rate is 4%. What is the swap's fair value to Harper?
exp: Expected net receipts are $1,000,000 x 1% = $10,000 per year; PV = $10,000/1.04 + $10,000/1.04^2 = $9,615 + $9,246 = $18,861. The $20,000 answer ignores discounting, and $19,231 discounts both payments for only one period.

q: Ingram Co. holds equity securities measured at fair value through net income. It purchased put options on the same securities as an economic hedge. During the year the securities declined $30,000 and the puts gained $26,000. What is the net effect on Ingram's net income?
choices: $30,000 decrease, with the $26,000 gain reported in OCI
exp: Both the equity securities (ASC 321) and the undesignated puts are measured at fair value through net income, so the net effect is -$30,000 + $26,000 = $4,000 decrease; hedge accounting is unnecessary and not permitted for items already remeasured through earnings. Putting the put gain in OCI wrongly applies cash flow hedge treatment.

q: Jarvis Corp. deferred a $50,000 gain in AOCI from a cash flow hedge of the forecasted purchase of equipment. The equipment was acquired on January 1 and is depreciated straight-line over 10 years with no salvage value. How much of the deferred gain is reclassified into earnings in the first year?
exp: The hedged forecasted purchase affects earnings through depreciation, so the gain is reclassified as an offset to depreciation over the asset's life: $50,000 / 10 = $5,000. Reclassifying the entire $50,000 at purchase ignores that buying equipment does not affect earnings.

q: Kessler Co. assesses hedge effectiveness using regression analysis. For a proposed hedge, the regression of changes in the derivative's value on changes in the hedged item's value produced a slope of -0.92 and an R-squared of 0.76. What is the appropriate conclusion?
choices: Highly effective, because the slope is within the -0.80 to -1.25 range
Not highly effective, because R-squared is below the generally accepted 0.80 threshold
Not highly effective, because the slope is negative
exp: Common practice requires both an R-squared of at least 0.80 and a slope between -0.80 and -1.25; the 0.76 R-squared fails even though the slope is acceptable. A negative slope is expected, since the derivative should move opposite to the hedged item.

q: Lawson Co. uses futures contracts designated as cash flow hedges of forecasted purchases of raw materials. The hedges do not contain an other-than-insignificant financing element. In the statement of cash flows, how should cash flows from settling the futures contracts be classified?
exp: ASC 230 permits cash flows from a derivative accounted for as a hedge to be classified in the same category as the cash flows of the hedged item—here, inventory purchases in operating activities. Investing is a common trap because derivatives are sometimes thought of as investments.

q: Morton Corp. issued $3,000,000 of fixed-rate debt at par and designated a receive-fixed, pay-variable swap as a fair value hedge. At year-end, benchmark rates had risen and the swap was a $45,000 liability; the decline in the debt's fair value attributable to the benchmark rate was also $45,000. What is the carrying amount of the debt at year-end?
exp: In a fair value hedge, the hedged debt's carrying amount is adjusted for the change in fair value attributable to the hedged risk: $3,000,000 - $45,000 = $2,955,000. Leaving the debt at $3,000,000 ignores the required basis adjustment, and $3,045,000 moves it in the wrong direction.
